newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel chief in Goma, rebels report advances.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel chief in Goma, rebels report advances.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila flew to the eastern city of Goma on Wednesday and a rebel spokesman rejected sharing power with ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko's political party.
Rebel Voice of the People radio claimed Kabila's forces were within 100 km (60 miles) both of Zaire's second largest city of Lubumbashi in the southeast and the diamond capital of Mbuji-Mayi.
Independent aid and expatriate sources told Reuters in Lubumbashi the rebels were further away than their radio claimed.
Witnesses said Kabila arrived in Goma by plane from the northeastern Zairean capital of Kisangani and was driven to his lakeside residence in this city bordering on Rwanda with a heavy rebel escort.
An official with the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation Congo-Zaire (ADFL) told Reuters Kabila had business in Goma before going to another location for a meeting.
He said Kabila would return to Kisangani in three days and he did not know where the rebel chief would go after Goma.
A rebel delegation was in Lome, Togo, for an Organisation of Africa Unity (OAU) summit on the Zaire crisis that opened on Wednesday. Kabila and President Mobutu Sese Seko were not expected in Togo.

Kabila arrived in Kisangani on Friday, six days after it was captured. Its fall was the biggest prize so far for AFDL, which has seized about a quarter of Africa's third largest country since October.

Voice of the People, broadcasting from Goma, said both Lubumbashi and Mbuji-Mayi were "within the grip" of the rebel forces, but did not give precise locations to where they had advanced. It was not possible to confirm the report.

Expatriates in Lubumbashi with contacts nearest to the no man's land between the rebels and Zairean forces said that at the present slow advance, it would be at least 10 days before Kabila's forces reached the city.
Aid workers said Zairean troops still held at least the southern part of Lake Mweru, 300 km (180 miles) from the city.
The ADFL has named Lubumbashi, the copper and cobalt mining capital of the southern mineral-rich region of Shaba, as its next major target, closely followed by Mbuji-Mayi south of Kisangani.
Asked about a proposal made on Tuesday by Mobutu's Popular Revolutionary Movement (MPR) for it and the ADFL to share power before elections, rebel information commissioner Raphael Nghenda said:
"There cannot be power-sharing between us and Mobutu's people. It is impossible."
Rebel officials said their delegation in Lome would explain their position on Zaire at the OAU summit but would not negotiate with the delegation sent by Mobutu.
A rebel delegation could in future hold talks with envoys of Mobutu to prepare for a summit between Mobutu and Kabila, rebel justice commissioner Mwanze Kongolo said on Tuesday.
He said South Africa was the ideal but not the only location for a meeting and he hoped preparatory talks would start soon.
In Lome, Bizima Karaha, Kabila's chief foreign policy strategist and a leader of the rebel team at the OAU meeting, also rejected power-sharing but said he believed negotiations might start soon.
"We shall never, never enter into any power-sharing with the government in Kinshasa. One thing for sure, we are not fighting for power-sharing," he told British Broadcasting Corporation radio.
